# Combat telemetry wire vectors (v1)

Generated by `wire_vectors.py` in this folder; do not edit by hand:

```
python wire_vectors.py > wire-vectors.md
```

The contract is section 4 of `../autoacc-backend-research.md`, with the ops
moved to 0xC0-0xCF (`../combat-telemetry.md`). The server codec
(`modules/custom/lua/combat_telemetry_wire.lua`, checked by
`tools/tests/combat_telemetry_wire.lua`) and dlac's codec reproduce every
frame here. Server frames (S2C) are shown as the client receives them.
Client frames (C2S) are shown as an addon hands them to `AddOutgoingPacket`,
with the first four header bytes left 0 for Ashita to fill, except TV-01w,
which is the same frame on the wire.

A slice-1 server and a THF 75 / DNC 37 with a dagger, a sword off hand and a
bow, fighting a level 78 mob. The worn items and their modifiers are the
real ones; the character's other stats are chosen by hand. Everything
derived from them is computed by the script with the server's rules: the
stats without gear, the accuracy composition and hit rate of section 1.8,
the threshold conversion, and every hash. Identity hashes are 0, the v1
rule.

## Formula vectors

The composition check: each line recomputes a published context from the published live totals, as dlac's formula check does (section 2.2). `skill` is GetAccFromSkill of the live SkillLevel; `stat` is floor(DEX or AGI x 0.75); `food` is the capped food term; `getACC` must equal the published LiveAcc; `eff` adds PolicyAccBonus, subtracts FlashPenalty and adds LevelCorrection. `product` is rate x 100 in doubles before the truncation.

```
TV-05 ctx 0: SkillLevel 256 -> skill 250, stat 66, base 353, food 30, getACC 383, eff 371 vs EVA 320 -> raw 10050 bp, product 95, threshold 95, AccToCap -11
TV-05 ctx 1: SkillLevel 190 -> skill 190, stat 66, base 293, food 29, getACC 322, eff 310 vs EVA 320 -> raw 7000 bp, product 70, threshold 70, AccToCap +50
TV-05 ctx 3: SkillLevel 128 -> skill 128, stat 60, base 218, food 22, getACC 240, eff 228 vs EVA 320 -> raw 2900 bp, product 28.999999999999996, threshold 28, AccToCap +132
TV-06 ctx 0: SkillLevel 256 -> skill 250, stat 69, base 349, food 30, getACC 379, eff 367 vs EVA 320 -> raw 9850 bp, product 95, threshold 95, AccToCap -7
TV-06 ctx 1: SkillLevel 190 -> skill 190, stat 69, base 289, food 28, getACC 317, eff 305 vs EVA 320 -> raw 6750 bp, product 67.5, threshold 67, AccToCap +55
TV-06 ctx 3: SkillLevel 128 -> skill 128, stat 60, base 218, food 22, getACC 240, eff 228 vs EVA 320 -> raw 2900 bp, product 28.999999999999996, threshold 28, AccToCap +132
```

The gear check: live - R per input is exactly the plain modifiers of the outfit named by EquipRev (set bonuses would add here; there are none).

```
TV-05 live - R: DEX 0, AGI 0, AccMod 17, RaccMod 10, TwoHandAccMod 0, WsAccMod 0
TV-06 live - R: DEX 2, AGI 0, AccMod 10, RaccMod 10, TwoHandAccMod 0, WsAccMod 0
```

The local projection dlac makes before releasing Toreador's Ring (2.2): TV-05's R, plus the plain modifiers and the active latents of the proposed outfit, gives TV-06's live totals, and the composition gives its contexts.

```
DEX: R 88 - worn latents 0 + Rajas Ring DEX+2 + its latents DEX+3 = 93 (TV-06 live 93)
AccMod: R 20 + Peacock Amulet ACC+10 = 30 (TV-06 live 30)
ctx 0: threshold 95 -> 95, AccToCap -11 -> -7
ctx 1: threshold 70 -> 67, AccToCap +50 -> +55
ctx 3: threshold 28 -> 28, AccToCap +132 -> +132
weapon skill, first hit (TV-05 main hand, no fTP gear): eff 371 + 100 + WSACC 0 + flourish 0 -> rate 0.95 (continuous roll, compared with the cap directly)
```

```
GetAccFromSkill(0) = 0
GetAccFromSkill(150) = 150
GetAccFromSkill(200) = 200
GetAccFromSkill(201) = 200
GetAccFromSkill(256) = 250
GetAccFromSkill(400) = 380
GetAccFromSkill(401) = 380
GetAccFromSkill(450) = 420
GetAccFromSkill(600) = 540
GetAccFromSkill(601) = 540
GetAccFromSkill(700) = 630
GetAccFromSkill: float (as compiled) and double agree for every skill 0..1500
food ACC term: trunc(float(ACC x pct) / 100.f) equals integer truncation for ACC 0..1200, pct 0..50
food RACC term, base 218, 10 %, cap 30: 22 (a plain 10 % would give 21)
```

## Hashes and the comparison key

```
FNV-1a32("") = 0x811C9DC5 (offset basis)
FNV-1a32("a") = 0xE40C292C (published reference value 0xE40C292C)
EquipRev(TV-05 outfit) = 0x78CAEAF2
EquipRev(TV-06 outfit) = 0xEBC50981
TV-05 with Rev 5, no FIRST, SampleMs +4000 and DistanceDeci 41: same key
TV-05 with Peacock Amulet taken off (a gear-only change, no latents): same key, so it publishes only if that outfit is new this session
TV-06: a different key (DEX R moved with the Rajas Ring latents)
```
